learningObjectives: Select and justify role-based access control (rbac) in a business scenario.
Select and justify permission inheritance and dependent roles in a business scenario.
Select and justify attachment categories in a business scenario.
Select and justify attribute-based access control (abac) security model in a business scenario.
Select and justify client-based access control in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines allowed operations. An Access Group selects application access and roles. RBAC assigns capabilities through roles, Access of Role to Object rules and privileges. Hiding a button alone is not server authorization.

elements.text: Worked example: A service representative can update customer requests, while a supervisor role has a separate approval privilege. Check direct action calls as well as portal visibility.

elements.description: Dependent roles reuse standard permissions while allowing targeted overrides. Parent-class permissions can be inherited by child classes. Inspect explicit grants/denials and dependent-role order; do not treat permission inheritance as an unconditional union of all permissions.

elements.text: Worked example: Start from the standard user role and override only the permission needed for a specialized case class. Test both the explicit override and inherited operations.

elements.description: Attachment categories organize documents and restrict attachment actions through privileges, When conditions and applicable team constraints. All configured When conditions must be true; at least one required privilege must be held. Use When rules for category conditions, not Access When rules.

elements.text: Worked example: Keep incident photos and restricted financial documents in separate categories. Grant read access to the intended role and verify create/edit/delete independently.

elements.description: ABAC supplements RBAC by comparing operator and object attributes for granular access. An Access Control Policy identifies the controlled action; an Access Control Policy Condition expresses the decision logic. Evaluate row and property restrictions in every relevant access path.

elements.text: Worked example: Only investigators whose region matches a case may read it. Compare operator region and case region in a policy condition, then apply the read policy.

elements.description: CBAC supports client requests to inspect, correct or erase their own personal data through a request-management application and participating repositories. Configure the permitted data and operations; CBAC is not ordinary role authorization or proof of legal compliance by itself.

elements.text: Worked example: A customer submits a correction request through the designated request-management flow. Validate identity, locate the configured personal data and apply the permitted correction.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: UI visibility
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A hidden approval button prevents all unauthorized calls.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Enforce authorization on the server operation.

examPitfalls.title: RBAC versus ABAC
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Roles alone express every object-specific attribute condition.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use ABAC where the decision depends on operator and object attributes.

examPitfalls.title: Category conditions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: One true When condition overrides other false conditions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: All category When conditions must be satisfied.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user has signed in successfully but must not approve refunds. Which concern decides approval access?

options.text: The portal's background color
The queue's display name
Authorization
Authentication alone

practiceQuiz.rationale: Authentication confirms identity. Authorization controls allowed actions after identity has been established.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Colors do not enforce approval permissions.
optionExplanations.B: Queue labels do not grant the approval action.
optionExplanations.C: Authorization determines permitted actions after sign-in.
optionExplanations.D: Identity verification alone does not grant approval rights.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An approval button is hidden for regular users. Which additional control is necessary?

options.text: No further check because hidden UI is sufficient
A server-enforced role or privilege check on approval
Only a smaller icon
Only a tooltip

practiceQuiz.rationale: Direct requests can bypass presentation. Authorization must protect the operation itself.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: A direct request can bypass a hidden button.
optionExplanations.B: Protect the approval operation with server authorization.
optionExplanations.C: Icon size is presentation, not permission enforcement.
optionExplanations.D: Tooltips do not prevent unauthorized requests.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A custom user role needs one exception while retaining standard capabilities. Which approach supports maintainability?

options.text: Use a dependent standard role with a targeted override
Copy every permission into unrelated roles indefinitely
Grant all developer privileges
Remove all class inheritance

practiceQuiz.rationale: Dependent roles reuse common permissions and let the application customize only the difference.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Dependent roles reuse common permissions with a focused override.
optionExplanations.B: Repeated copies increase maintenance and divergence.
optionExplanations.C: Developer privileges exceed the stated exception.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An attachment category has two When conditions and a required privilege. One When condition is false. May the user perform the action solely because they hold the privilege?

options.text: Yes; privileges bypass category conditions
Yes; attachments have no access control
Only the file extension decides
No; all configured When conditions must also be true

practiceQuiz.rationale: Category authorization combines the required privilege and condition constraints. A false required condition blocks the action.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: A privilege does not bypass required When conditions.
optionExplanations.C: Extensions alone do not establish action authorization.
optionExplanations.D: The false required condition blocks the configured action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team needs different access for photographs and salary documents attached to cases. Which mechanism fits?

options.text: A new ruleset patch for every file
One public URL with no controls
Separate attachment categories with appropriate privileges and conditions
A higher assignment urgency for salary files

practiceQuiz.rationale: Categories organize attachment types and provide category-level action restrictions.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: File-specific patches are not category access controls.
optionExplanations.B: An uncontrolled public URL cannot separate permissions.
optionExplanations.C: Categories allow different privileges and conditions per document type.
optionExplanations.D: Urgency does not protect salary documents.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Access should depend on whether a case's classification is within the operator's clearance. Which model fits?

options.text: A field-value translation alone
ABAC with a policy and policy condition
Authentication alone
A static portal title

practiceQuiz.rationale: ABAC compares object attributes with user attributes, enabling granular access beyond membership in a role.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Translations do not compare security attributes.
optionExplanations.B: ABAC conditions can compare operator clearance with Case classification.
optionExplanations.C: Identity alone does not evaluate attribute restrictions.
optionExplanations.D: Titles do not enforce object-level access.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO responsibilities are separated in ABAC configuration?

options.text: A policy identifies the controlled action
A policy condition evaluates relevant attributes
A theme decides server access
A work queue replaces identity verification

practiceQuiz.rationale: Policy and policy condition separate the protected action from the comparison logic used to decide access.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: The policy identifies the protected action.
optionExplanations.B: The condition evaluates the relevant attributes.
optionExplanations.C: A theme cannot enforce server permissions.
optionExplanations.D: A queue does not replace identity checks.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Customers need a configured workflow to request corrections to their own stored personal data. Which mechanism is most directly relevant?

options.text: Role-based access control alone
Field-level auditing alone
An attachment category alone
Client-based access control

practiceQuiz.rationale: CBAC provides a framework for client personal-data requests. It still requires identity and operation-specific configuration.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: RBAC alone is not the client-request framework.
optionExplanations.B: Auditing records changes, not personal-data request orchestration.
optionExplanations.C: Attachment categories govern files, not the overall request workflow.
optionExplanations.D: CBAC supports configured personal-data request processing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A dependent-role list contains different explicit decisions for one class. Which detail must be reviewed?

options.text: Only the operator's division
Only the portal the user opens
The dependent-role order and the application's explicit overrides
Only the most permissive decision anywhere in the list

practiceQuiz.rationale: Dependent-role evaluation is not an unconditional union of all grants. Order and explicit permissions affect the result.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Division alone does not resolve explicit dependent-role decisions.
optionExplanations.B: Portal choice alone does not resolve role ordering.
optionExplanations.C: Order and explicit overrides affect the applicable permission decision.
optionExplanations.D: Evaluation is not an unconditional union of all grants.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Does implementing a personal-data request framework alone prove that every regulatory requirement is satisfied?

options.text: Yes; client requests never need identity checks
No; the framework must be configured and evaluated against the actual requirements
Yes; configuring CBAC certifies the whole application
Yes; CBAC eliminates retention policies

practiceQuiz.rationale: CBAC supports a class of personal-data operations. Broader obligations and operation-specific safeguards still require evaluation.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Personal-data requests still require identity safeguards.
optionExplanations.B: Evaluate the configured workflow against its actual requirements.
optionExplanations.C: Framework adoption is not a compliance certification.

quickRecap.value: Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines allowed operations. An Access Group selects application access and roles. RBAC assigns capabilities through roles, Access of Role to Object rules and privileges. Hiding a button alone is not server authorization.

Dependent roles reuse standard permissions while allowing targeted overrides. Parent-class permissions can be inherited by child classes. Inspect explicit grants/denials and dependent-role order; do not treat permission inheritance as an unconditional union of all permissions.

Attachment categories organize documents and restrict attachment actions through privileges, When conditions and applicable team constraints. All configured When conditions must be true; at least one required privilege must be held. Use When rules for category conditions, not Access When rules.

ABAC supplements RBAC by comparing operator and object attributes for granular access. An Access Control Policy identifies the controlled action; an Access Control Policy Condition expresses the decision logic. Evaluate row and property restrictions in every relevant access path.

CBAC supports client requests to inspect, correct or erase their own personal data through a request-management application and participating repositories. Configure the permitted data and operations; CBAC is not ordinary role authorization or proof of legal compliance by itself.
